markscheme.html:
3a

Specific heat capacity is the energy required to raise the temperature of one kilogram of a material by one kelvin. 

Specific latent heat is the energy required to change the phase of one kilogram of a material without changing its temperature.

3b(i)

Let's represent the mass of an ice cube by m.

Energy required to change the temperature of the ice from -5 C to 0 C:

(5m)(2100)(5) = 52500m

Energy required to melt the ice:

(5m)(0.37 10) = 1850000m

Energy required to change the temperature of the melted ice from 0 C to 14 C:

(5m)(4200)(14) = 294000m

Total energy required by the ice during the process: 2196500m

Energy lost by the water when cooling from 32 C to 14 C:

(0.52)(4200)(18) = 39312 J

Equating energy values:

2196500m = 39312

m = 0.017898 kg 0.018 kg or 18 g

Answer must be given to 2 s. f. to earn final mark.

3b(ii)

Not all the energy from the cooling water is transferred to the ice. As a result, the specific latent heat of fusion value calculated based on the experiment is higher than the actual value.

3c(i)

It takes less time for the crushed ice to melt (because its surface area is larger than that of the ice cubes).

3c(ii)

The estimated specific latent heat value will be the same (because the same amount of energy is transferred to the ice in both cases).

question.html:
A student carries out an experiment to determine the specific latent heat of fusion of ice. She drops five ice cubes into a container filled with water. 

The following data is available for the experiment:

Initial temperature of the ice cubes: -5.0 C

Initial temperature of the water: 32 C

Final temperature of the water: 14 C

Mass of water: 520 g

Specific heat capacity of water: 4.2 kJ kg K

Specific heat capacity of ice: 2.1 kJ kg K

Estimated value of specific latent heat of fusion of ice based on the experiment: 0.37 MJ kg

a. Distinguish between specific heat capacity and specific latent heat.

  [2]

b. After carrying out the experiment, the student realizes that she did not measure the mass of the ice cubes.

i. Find an estimate for the mass of one ice cube. Give your answer to an appropriate number of significant figures.

  [5]

ii. State and explain why the value of the specific latent heat of fusion of ice based on the student's calculations is an estimate.

  [2]

c. In a similar experiment the same amount of crushed ice is used. Suggest how using crushed ice affects:

i. The time taken for the ice to completely melt.

  [1]

ii. The estimated value of the specific latent heat of fusion of ice.

  [1]
